[Thinking]
**Reconstructing a story**

I need to write a story based on a prompt, and it looks like I’ll likely need to reconstruct an article. I think I’ll break it down into five sections to keep everything organized. This will help me cover all the key points effectively. Okay, let’s get started on structuring the sections so they flow well together! It’s really important to create a cohesive narrative that makes sense.
[/Thinking]

Section 1  
The health secretary, Jeremy Hunt, has found himself at the centre of an unusual Twitter confrontation with comedy actor Ralf Little over claims about the state of NHS mental healthcare. The dispute began after Hunt appeared on The Andrew Marr Show and said the NHS had overseen “the biggest expansion of mental health provision in Europe.” Little, who is best known for playing Anthony in The Royle Family, reacted strongly to the statement, accusing Hunt in a tweet of “knowingly lying” to the public about the statistics.

Section 2  
Little’s challenge escalated the row when he told Hunt to sue him if he was wrong. The health secretary, who had recently been forced to backtrack on a claim to parliament that there had been an increase of 30,000 mental health workers — a figure later shown to be 43 times the actual number — responded a week later with a series of statistics and “double dared” Little to prove him wrong. Hunt’s reply did little to calm the situation, instead turning the exchange into a public test of each side’s numbers and credibility.

Section 3  
In response, Little posted a thread of more than 40 tweets setting out his rebuttal of Hunt’s claims. He included statistics from Full Fact, the independent UK fact-checking charity, in an effort to challenge the health secretary’s account of NHS progress. The thread was widely circulated and had been shared more than 15,000 times, turning what began as a brief exchange into a much larger online argument about mental health staffing, funding, and political honesty.

Section 4  
The dispute continued on Monday when Hunt replied with a long thread of 26 tweets of his own. At points he lost track of the chronology, making the exchange difficult to follow, but he continued to press Little for evidence. “Now I know you are a funny bloke and in politics a lot of insults are traded but the question is can you back up what is a very strong claim?” he wrote, addressing Little’s accusation that he had been lying to the public. Hunt also pointed to measures his department had taken to address staffing shortages in mental health services.

Section 5  
Among the examples Hunt cited was the claim that the NHS now has 8,000 mental health nurses in training and that, in September, the government announced a 25% increase in nurse training places overall. He also referenced a New York Times article from July, noting that it had been corrected three times after Luciana Berger, the former shadow minister for mental health, challenged its contents. Despite his efforts to defend his record, the row has continued to grow, illustrating both the sensitivity of NHS mental health policy and the speed with which political disputes can spread on social media.
